name: Rwanda
summary: Children and spouse have a reserved share. Gifts cannot exceed one fifth of the estate if the donor has children (four fifths reserved for children and spouse); with no children but a spouse, the free share is one third. A foreigner's will is governed as to substance by the law of their country of origin (art. 70).
reserved_share: Law 27/2016, art. 49: with children, the disposable portion is at most 1/5 and 4/5 is the reserved portion of children and spouse; with no children but a living spouse, the disposable portion is at most 1/3 and 2/3 is the spouse's reserved portion. Art. 48 defines the disposable portion.
foreign_law_note: Law 27/2016, art. 70: wills made by a foreigner residing in Rwanda are governed as to form by the law of the place made (or the foreigner's national law) and as to substance and effects by the law of the country of origin. Art. 50 lets foreign parties choose another law for donations, subject to Rwandan public order.
trust_note: No trust or private-foundation law was found; answers provisional.
open_questions: A newer family law (Law 71/2024) may have replaced or amended Law 27/2016; check whether arts. 48-49 and 70 survive.
Whether art. 70 country-of-origin law removes forced heirship in practice is untested.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
